subject: forestry
intro: Forestry manages forests for timber, habitat and climate, and it leads to work measuring stands, planning harvests, preventing wildfire and teaching the science of the woods.

roles.title: Foresters
roles.what: Manage forested lands for economic, recreational and conservation purposes: inventory standing timber, appraise its worth, negotiate purchases, plan regeneration, monitor growth and set harvesting schedules while protecting soil, water and habitat.
roles.where: Forest mensuration's inventory, sampling and growth modelling, silviculture's regeneration methods, and the sustained-yield and rotation logic of the management unit are the daily instruments of the job.

roles.title: Conservation Scientists
roles.what: Manage, improve and protect natural resources to maximise their use without damaging the environment, planning against soil erosion and advising land managers on practices that keep land productive.
roles.where: Forest ecology's succession and disturbance, the soils and nutrient-cycles topics, and the policy unit's conservation and climate strand supply the resource-management reasoning the role needs.

roles.title: Forest Fire Inspectors and Prevention Specialists
roles.what: Enforce fire regulations, inspect forests for fire hazards, recommend prevention and control measures, and report forest fires and weather conditions.
roles.where: The fire ecology and management topic in the forest-health unit, plus the disturbance dynamics of the forest-ecology unit, is precisely the hazard assessment this role performs in the field.

roles.title: Forestry and Conservation Science Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach courses in forestry and conservation science, combining classroom teaching with research into the forests, stands and ecosystems they cover.
roles.where: This SAF-accredited arc — ecology, mensuration, silviculture, management, health and policy — mirrors the structure of accredited forestry degrees you would go on to teach.
